CausalChain: Boronated nanoparticles accumulate selectively in tumor cells -> BNCT irradiation induces high LET radiation causing localized DNA damage and immunogenic cell death -> Tumor cell death releases damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) and tumor antigens -> Conjugated TLR agonist signals locally enhance dendritic cell activation -> Enhanced antigen presentation drives robust T-cell mediated antitumor immunity -> Systemic immune response may elicit abscopal effects
Hypothesis: The co-delivery of boronated nanoparticles conjugated with TLR agonists in BNCT not only augments localized tumor cell killing but also stimulates a systemic antitumor immune response, thereby improving therapeutic outcomes and enabling potential abscopal effects in otherwise treatment-resistant cancers.
Abstract: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) delivers high‐LET radiation in a tumor‐selective manner and has shown promise in treating a variety of malignancies; however, its clinical utility is limited by localized toxicities and a lack of systemic immune engagement. We propose a novel strategy wherein boronated nanoparticles are conjugated with Toll‐like receptor (TLR) agonists to not only achieve selective tumor boron accumulation but also to stimulate innate immune activation upon BNCT-induced tumor cell kill. This dual-function approach is hypothesized to enhance dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation, thereby amplifying antitumor T-cell responses and potentially inducing abscopal effects. Our hypothesis integrates radiation‐induced immunogenic cell death originating from BNCT with targeted immune activation to overcome immune escape mechanisms and improve overall therapeutic outcomes.
